title: A Hymn for the Visitor
premise: Tamsin Quintana, a rationalist teacher fleeing a scandal, takes a post in the isolated village of Hollowmere, where children have been vanishing from class rolls for generations and no one will say why. When a bell that was melted down in 1911 begins ringing at dusk, Tamsin learns the village has been paying an annual tithe to something the founders invited in—a bargain renewed each year with a child. Refusing to let his students be chosen, Tamsin uncovers the original covenant hidden in the church records and realizes the entity can only take what is freely surrendered; the horror culminates at sunrise when he offers himself in place of the chosen girl, breaking the contract's terms and unmaking the visitor—but only by accepting that survival always costs someone, and this time it must cost him everything he believed about staying safe.
about_author: Noor Brightwater is a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in coastal villages where old agreements were never written down but always honored. She writes horror about institutions that protect themselves instead of their children.

chapters.title: The Roll Call of Absences
chapters.summary: Tamsin arrives in Hollowmere and takes over a classroom whose register lists eleven enrolled pupils but seats only eight. The headmaster warns him not to ask about the gaps. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity masked as professional detachment.

chapters.title: What the Melted Bell Remembers
chapters.summary: At dusk a bell tolls though locals confirm it was melted for scrap in 1911. Tamsin investigates the empty belfry and finds fresh rope fiber and wax. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: first crack in his disbelief, dread taking root.

chapters.title: Children Who Count Themselves Carefully
chapters.summary: A student, Wren, tells him the missing children 'went to sing' and that everyone takes turns eventually. Her matter-of-fact terror unsettles him more than any ghost story could. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: protective instinct awakening.

chapters.title: The Minutes of 1911
chapters.summary: In the church archive Tamsin finds parish minutes describing a 'Visitor' invited by the founding families after a famine, promised one voice per year in exchange for the village's survival. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: horror of complicity—the whole village is guilty.

chapters.title: Everyone Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts the headmaster and the vicar; they admit the tithe but insist it keeps forty families alive and fed through winters that would otherwise kill them. POV: alternating Tamsin and vicar's confession. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—justice outside the law looks like murder.

chapters.title: Wren's Name on the List
chapters.summary: The village draws lots in secret; Wren is chosen. Her found-family of classmates begs Tamsin to do nothing, terrified that interference dooms them all. POV: Wren briefly, then Tamsin. Emotional beat: heartbreak and the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: The Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Tamsin rereads the covenant and finds the loophole: the Visitor may accept any willing voice offered freely in substitution, but a broken promise curses the giver. He decides. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Nightfall at the Belfry
chapters.summary: Tamsin locks the school, sends Wren away, and climbs to the belfry as the melted bell begins to swing. The Visitor arrives wearing the accumulated faces of every child it took. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: A Hymn for the Visitor
chapters.summary: Climax: Tamsin sings the hymn the missing children once sang, offering himself freely. The Visitor, bound by the covenant's own words, cannot refuse—and a gift given without coercion voids the original invitation. The bell cracks mid-toll. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: transcendence inside horror.

chapters.title: Sunrise, and the Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Dawn finds the belfry empty and the register complete—every absent name crossed out and returned. Wren inherits Tamsin's classroom and his refusal to look away, vowing the village will never sign again. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief braided with hope; found family endures the cost.
